inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, FY2025 10-K cash-flow-statement add-back ($321.56M) plus 9M FY2026 10-Qs; FY2026E built from 9M actual ($266.6M, Q3 estimated pro-rata on the H1 SBC/revenue ratio since ADI does not disclose single-quarter SBC) plus Q4 guided-revenue x H1 SBC-of-revenue ratio (2.47%). ADI does not separately disclose cash tax withheld on net-share settlement in a distinct XBRL tag; the cash-flow add-back is used as the combined figure per the fallback rule.
inputs.wacc_rationale: US risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST) + beta 1.15 x ERP 5.0% = ~10.0% cost of equity; negligible debt weight (D/(D+E)~4%) at ~4% after-tax cost of debt (investment-grade, ~5% pretax, 20% effective tax) blends to ~9.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios -- cyclicality is charged through the scenario paths and probability weights, not stacked again as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- ADI's lease liabilities are immaterial relative to total debt; no separate lease adjustment made
inputs.notes: Standard operating company (semiconductor manufacturer) -- owner-FCF DCF via SKILL.md routing table, no adaptations file needed (US filer). FY0 is NOT the last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended 2025-11-01) but a built FY2026E: 9-month actuals (Q1-Q3 FY2026, ended 2026-08-01) plus the company's own Q4 FY2026 guidance (revenue $4.3B +/- $100M, adj. operating margin 52% +/- 100bps, adj. gross margin ~74%), because FY2026 is 92% complete and guidance is explicit and recent (2026-08-19 earnings call). This avoids anchoring the model to a fiscal year that ended eleven months ago while the business has grown +37% YoY since. FY2026E revenue = $15,105.6M (9M actual $10,805.6M + Q4 guided midpoint $4,300M), +37.1% YoY over FY2025's $11,019.7M -- this base-year growth rate is NOT projected forward; it is the historical/guided anchor the year-1 (FY2027) growth rate of 20% (management's own 'at least 20%' framing) decelerates from. Historical revenue/EPS/equity CAGRs are not usable un-adjusted: FY2022-23 were a cyclical, M&A-inflated peak (Maxim all-stock merger closed FY2021, stepping equity from ~$8B to ~$38B in one year with no organic driver), FY2024 was the trough (-24% revenue peak-to-trough per Analysis JSON), so 3yr CAGRs are negative and the 5yr equity CAGR (23%) is a one-off M&A artifact, not organic compounding -- growth_divergence_warning set accordingly and the forward path is anchored to management guidance and unit-economics (AI datacenter content $ per GW, industrial recovery breadth) from the Analysis JSON instead of a blended historical CAGR. D&A carries heavy acquisition-intangible amortization from Maxim/Linear step-ups ($1.59B of FY2025's $1.999B total D&A, 14.4% of revenue) on a run-off schedule -- modelled declining from 16% of revenue to a normalized ~4% (depreciation-only) by year 6 as those intangibles fully amortize; this is a real, disclosed, terminal decline, not an assumed one. Cash effective tax rate has risen from 8.0% (FY2024) to 16.4% (FY2025) as one-off credits/valuation allowances used up; ramped to 20% by year 7 (still below the 21% federal statutory rate given ADI's persistent R&D credit and foreign-manufacturing-mix benefits, but not held at the currently-low rate in perpetuity). Working capital modelled with wc_capture_pct negative (-8%) in all scenarios -- ADI is a physical-inventory manufacturer/distributor, not a deferred-revenue SaaS business, so growth consumes cash in receivables and inventory (confirmed by the FY2023 upcycle showing a large negative OCF-vs-NI+D&A+SBC gap). Terminal cap multiple set at 16x, between the house default 20x compounder cap and the 12-15x cyclical floor, reflecting ADI's genuine secular content-growth tailwinds (auto electrification, AI datacenter) layered on real cyclicality. Horizon is 10 years because the year-5 EBITDA margin (50.0% base case) is still short of the assumed mature level (51.0%) and D&A is still tapering from the acquisition-amortization run-off at year 5.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management guidance (FY2027 'at least 20% growth'), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All CAGR measures are distorted and NOT used as the forward growth anchor. 3yr CAGRs (revenue -2.8%, EPS -4.6%, equity -2.5%) are negative purely because FY2022-23 were a cyclical, Maxim-merger-inflated peak and FY2024 was the post-COVID inventory-correction trough (revenue fell ~24% peak-to-trough per Analysis JSON) -- a mechanical artifact of where the 3-year window starts, not a growth signal. The 5yr equity CAGR (23.0%) is inflated by the one-off all-stock Maxim merger (FY2021 equity jumped from ~$8B to ~$38B on share issuance, not organic retained earnings), so it overstates organic compounding. The FCF 5yr CAGR (15.9% owner-FCF-basis) is the least distorted of the historical measures but still spans the same M&A/cyclical noise. Forward growth is instead anchored to management's own FY2027 guidance and the Analysis JSON's disclosed unit economics (AI datacenter content per GW of new capacity, industrial end-market recovery breadth).

base.narrative: Cyclical recovery in Industrial (49% of revenue) and Automotive (25%) continues broadening through FY2027-28 as the post-2023 inventory correction fully unwinds, layered with the AI datacenter power/connectivity ramp (Communications, 16% of revenue, growing >90% YoY) continuing for several years as management describes, before both decelerate toward a mature high-single-digit/low-double-digit blended growth rate as the AI buildout matures and industrial reverts to a GDP-plus content-growth cadence. Margins expand from the current cyclical trough toward management's guided run-rate (Q4 FY2026 non-GAAP operating margin 52%) and a mature ~51% EBITDA margin as fixed-cost absorption and mix shift toward higher-margin data-center/industrial products continue. Bolt-on M&A (Empower, pending Alif) is treated as sustaining, not incremental to, the base growth path.

bull.narrative: The CEO's framing that 'the broader analog industry could sustain double-digit growth for several years' proves right: AI datacenter power/connectivity content (currently $1-1.5B of analog content per new GW) grows further as hyperscaler capex compounds and ADI's optical/power attach rate rises, while Industrial and Automotive electrification/ADAS content growth runs hotter and longer than the base case as the current upcycle turns out to be structural rather than a normal inventory-driven cycle. Bolt-on M&A (Alif's edge-AI microcontrollers) adds a genuinely incremental TAM rather than merely sustaining growth. Capacity investment (capex ticks up) is required to meet demand, funded by materially higher operating leverage as gross margin clears 74%+ sustainably.

bear.narrative: The current upcycle proves to be an ordinary inventory/AI-capex-driven bulge rather than a structural step-change: a digestion phase in hyperscaler AI datacenter capex (the same concentration risk the Analysis JSON flags -- growth increasingly depends on a handful of hyperscale customers) coincides with a renewed industrial/automotive inventory correction similar to FY2023-FY2024's, cutting growth sharply in years 2-3 before a modest recovery. Texas Instruments' aggressive 300mm capacity expansion pressures pricing and share in overlapping analog lines through the downturn, compressing margins further than a normal cyclical trough (EBITDA margin falls to the mid-30s versus the FY2024 actual GAAP EBITDA margin of ~38%). China indigenization and export-control friction structurally shave share in a historically important geographic market, capping the eventual recovery below the base case's growth and margin levels.

scenario_narratives.base: Cyclical recovery in Industrial and Automotive continues broadening while the AI datacenter power/connectivity ramp persists for several years as management describes, both decelerating toward a mature high-single-digit blended growth rate as the AI buildout matures; margins expand toward the guided ~51-52% run-rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: The current upcycle is structural, not merely cyclical: AI datacenter content per GW keeps rising, industrial/auto electrification content growth runs hotter and longer, and bolt-on M&A (Alif) adds genuinely incremental TAM -- multi-year double-digit growth as the CEO has suggested is possible for the analog industry broadly.
scenario_narratives.bear: A digestion phase in concentrated hyperscaler AI capex coincides with a repeat of the FY2023-2024-style industrial/automotive inventory correction, compounded by Texas Instruments' capacity-driven pricing pressure and continuing China indigenization/export-control friction -- growth and margins fall sharply in years 2-3 before a muted recovery to a lower structural growth and margin plateau than the base case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the house default 15% to 25% because ADI's own 10-year history contains a real, recent instance of exactly this risk materializing (revenue fell ~24% peak-to-trough FY2023-FY2024) and the current growth is increasingly concentrated in a handful of hyperscale AI customers per the Analysis JSON's own concentration-risk flag -- this is not a generic downside, it is a demonstrated, repeatable pattern for this specific business. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously (AI capex sustains, industrial/auto content growth accelerates further, Alif/M&A integration executes cleanly) rather than one clean catalyst; base holds the default 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Analog Devices is a high-quality, diversified analog/mixed-signal semiconductor franchise with genuine design-in switching-cost moats, currently riding both a cyclical industrial/automotive recovery and a secular AI-datacenter power/connectivity growth wave simultaneously -- an unusually favorable but also unusually well-priced combination. The stock trades at roughly 12.8x the FY2026E guided revenue base and ~43x owner FCF, pricing in sustained elevated growth for years. The valuation below is built on management's own explicit FY2026 guidance and FY2027 growth framing rather than distorted historical CAGRs (the trailing 3-year window spans a full cyclical peak-to-trough-to-recovery cycle and an M&A-inflated equity base), decelerating toward a mature, still-attractive but no longer extraordinary growth and margin profile.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI datacenter capex digestion: growth is increasingly concentrated in a handful of hyperscale customers whose spending plans could shift quickly
Repeat of the FY2023-2024 industrial/automotive inventory correction -- ADI's own recent history shows a 24% peak-to-trough revenue swing is a real, not theoretical, risk
Texas Instruments' aggressive 300mm owned-fab capacity expansion pressuring pricing and share in overlapping analog product lines
US-China trade tensions, export controls and China's semiconductor indigenization push structurally eroding a historically important geographic market
Integration risk from a rapid cadence of acquisitions (Maxim, Empower, pending Alif) distracting management or diluting returns if the growth cycle decelerates before synergies are realized
